summary: The prepared base did not allow schedule_policy through SetInternalStateReq or Scheduler.set_internal_state. The change accepts string-valued controls, validates schedule_policy against the CacheAwarePolicy and CacheAgnosticPolicy enum values, and replaces only the scheduler's SchedulePolicy object in its synchronous control handler between scheduling passes. Existing waiting/running request containers and the prefix cache are retained. Unit coverage verifies enum acceptance, rejection without side effects, retained object identity, and changed LOF ordering. A private one-GPU HTTP run verified all enum values, invalid rejection, concurrent updates during generation, unchanged startup identity, and a 15-token device-cache hit after switching.

tests.what_was_measured: msgspec round trip for mixed string and numeric internal-state controls; 1 passed
all actual policy enum values accepted, invalid value rejected without mutation, waiting/running/cache identities preserved, and LOF reordered the existing queue in place; 3 passed
existing schedule-policy behavior plus runtime transition regression; 6 passed

real HTTP control path on one MI350X: seven accepted enum values, invalid rejection, four concurrent updates during a 96-token generation, unchanged startup_time, and 15 cached device tokens after policy switches

gpu_evidence: reports/j-326f6c074471/evidence/http/http-probe.json and server.log record execution on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950); gpu-before.csv and gpu-after.csv retain device identity and memory readings. The repeated prompt reported cached_tokens=15 after live policy updates.
remaining_limitations: The deterministic tiny random Llama validates transport, scheduler control, cache retention, and engine execution only; it does not validate semantic accuracy or another model architecture.

No distributed TP8 workload or GLM-5.2-NVFP4 model was available, so the source B300 production-traffic latency, starvation, 115K-token input, and 96% cache-hit measurements were not reproduced or claimed as current AMD measurements.
The concurrent HTTP updates were accepted and serialized by the scheduler control loop, but final-policy order is intentionally nondeterministic among concurrent callers.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild or compiler/ISA claim applies.
The prepared environment did not contain ruff or black; targeted tests, py_compile, and git diff --check passed.
